title: virtkit development environment
description: `.virtkit/config.toml`: a project's development environments, and the machine-local `.virtkit/local.toml` layer over it. Every key is checked; an unknown one is an error. The tracked file states `schema` and gives each environment exactly one source — `compose` (with `service`), `image` or `build`; a local layer states neither, since it only overrides what the tracked file says.

schema.description: the schema version; required in the tracked file

remove.description: local overrides only: dotted paths to drop from the inherited config before this layer applies, such as `dev.compose`

env-files.description: local overrides only: further env files, read after `local.env`, relative to the workspace root

environments.description: further named environments, selected with `--environment`; each stands alone and inherits nothing from `dev`

requires.title: requires
requires.description: what this project needs of the `vk` reading it

min-version.description: the oldest release that implements everything the config uses

features.description: `vk check --feature` names the build must answer for

environment.title: environment
environment.description: one environment: exactly one source — `compose` with `service`, `image`, or `build` — and how to be in it

compose.description: a compose file, relative to the workspace root; the environment is one of its services

service.description: the compose service to work in — the primary VM

image.description: an image reference, for an environment with no service LAN

build.description: a Dockerfile target, for an environment built from the project

cached-only.description: take the image from the build cache and never build it; with `fallback`, a cache miss runs the fallback target instead. A `build` source only.

fallback.description: what to build when `cached-only` misses the cache

workspace.description: where the workspace is mounted in the guest (an absolute guest path)

user.description: the user exec, shell and SSH sessions run as

freshness.description: what to do when the running environment no longer matches the config

profiles.description: compose profiles activated eagerly, besides the primary's dependencies

cpus.description: vCPUs for the primary: a count, or `"host"` for as many as the host has. Unset inherits the compose service's `x-virtkit.cpus`, then vk's default.

mem.description: memory for the primary (`16G`); unset inherits like `cpus`

exec-env.description: environment for development sessions: exec, shell, SSH and editor processes

container-env.description: environment for the guest's own processes, set at boot

mounts.description: extra host directories or files in the guest, by name

endpoints.description: guest ports published on the host, by name

tasks.description: project commands `vk dev task <name>` runs, by name

context.description: the build context, relative to the workspace root; required once layered

dockerfile.description: the Dockerfile, relative to the context (default `Dockerfile`)

target.description: the stage to boot (default: the last one)

args.description: `--build-arg` values for the build, by name

fallback.title: fallback
fallback.description: the smaller stage a `cached-only` environment builds when its own is not in the cache

target.description: the Dockerfile stage to build instead; required once layered

task.title: task
task.description: `[dev.tasks.<name>]`: a project command, and where and how it is executed

run.description: a shell string or an argv list, run in the workspace folder; required once layered

environment.description: where it runs: `dev` (default), or a name under `[environments]`

reuse.description: which running environment the reusing policies attach to, when that is not the one an ephemeral run would boot (default: `environment`)

checkout.description: how the checkout reaches the guest for this task

env.description: added to the environment's `exec-env` for this task

enabled.description: `false` in a local layer switches an inherited task off

policy.description: what a task does about the environment it needs: `reuse` attaches to a running one and fails when none runs, `require` boots it first, `ephemeral` boots a throwaway VM, `reuse-or-ephemeral` takes the running one when there is one

checkout-mode.description: what a task sees of the checkout: `shared` is the host's tree written through (the default), `overlay` a tmpfs over it whose writes go with the VM

freshness.description: `ask` offers a refresh on a terminal, `reuse` attaches and reports the differences, `refresh` rebuilds and replaces, `require-current` fails naming them

mount.title: mount
mount.description: `[dev.mounts.<name>]`: a host path in the guest

source.description: the host path; `~`, `${HOME}`, `${workspace}`, `${state}`, `${VK_UID}`, `${VK_GID}` and `${localEnv:NAME}` (or `${localEnv:NAME:default}`) are expanded. Required once layered.

to.description: the guest path (absolute); required once layered

optional.description: skip the mount when the source does not exist, rather than failing the boot

enabled.description: `false` in a local layer switches an inherited mount off

vscode.title: vscode
vscode.description: `[dev.editor.vscode]`: the managed VS Code server state and how it is reconciled

state.description: `persistent` keeps the server and its extensions across refreshes in managed storage; `ephemeral` lets them go with the environment generation

home.description: the user's home in the guest, where the server data directory lives; default `/root` for root and `/home/<user>` otherwise

reconcile.description: a project command run in the guest once the editor server is up, after the imported settings and extensions are applied

extensions.description: extensions to install in the remote

settings.description: remote settings to apply, without touching unrelated user preferences

host.title: host
host.description: `[dev.host]`: what the guest may reach on the host. Everything here is off by default.

git-gui.description: the built-in Git GUI policy: `gitk` and `git gui` on the host, over the mapped workspace, with their arguments and environment filtered

ssh-agent.description: forward the host's SSH agent into the guest

wrapper.description: a project's own host-command dispatcher, relative to the workspace root — the escape hatch for what the built-in policies do not cover

wrapper-env.description: environment variable patterns passed through to the wrapper

endpoint.title: endpoint
endpoint.description: `[dev.endpoints.<name>]`: one guest port, published on the host

service.description: the compose service that listens (default: the primary)

target.description: the guest port; required once layered

host-port.description: the preferred host port (default: the same number)

address.description: the host address: `auto` for a stable loopback allocation, or an address

scheme.description: for `vk dev open`: the URL scheme …

required.description: the environment is not ready until this is published

enabled.description: `false` in a local layer switches an inherited endpoint off

egress.description: `unrestricted` (default): the guest reaches what the host reaches; restricting it is not implemented

hooks.title: hooks
hooks.description: `[dev.hooks]`: when project commands run around the environment

init.description: on the host, from the workspace, before every build or start attempt

create.description: in the guest, once per materialized environment generation

start.description: in the guest, on each actual start — not on a reused attachment

hook.description: a hook in any of its forms: a shell string, an argv array, a table with `run` and its options, or a table of named hooks that run as a group (in turn; the group fails if any required member does). A named member cannot be called `run`, `cwd`, `timeout` or `required`.

run.description: a shell string or an argv array; required once layered

required.description: a failure fails the operation (default), or is reported and lets it continue

command.description: a shell string, or an argv list run directly
